panels.rationale: Contrast CT from case report of late-onset Schmidt's syndrome (APS type 2) showing atrophic adrenal glands leading to diagnosis of autoimmune adrenal disease. Caption and in-text explicitly attribute atrophy to this patient. Matches vocabulary adrenal_atrophy.

in_text_mentions: e patient excreted two loose stools. Cardiovascular measurements revealed mild hypotension (BP=105/58 mm Hg) and sinus rhythm on the very edge of tachycardia (HR=96 bpm). Considering the set of hypocortisolism symptoms, immediate treatment with i.v. hydrocortisone was started. The next day, the patient reported a substantial improvement in pain management and a better state of being. Furthermore, serum sodium concentration exceeded 135 mmol/l and neurological ailments resolved. Contrast CT imaging unveiled atrophic morphology of the adrenal glands (figure 1), which led to the diagnosis of aAD.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Axial abdominal CT from a patient with autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome type 2 demonstrates reduced volume of the right adrenal gland, supporting bilateral adrenal cortical atrophy associated with autoimmune adrenal insufficiency. B: Axial abdominal CT from a patient with autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome type 2 demonstrates reduced volume of the left adrenal gland, supporting bilateral adrenal cortical atrophy associated with autoimmune adrenal insufficiency.

findings.label: Diffuse bronze-brown skin hyperpigmentation
findings.evidence: generalized hyperpigmentation, darkening of creases on the palms of the hand

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Clinical photograph of patient palms showing diffuse hyperpigmentation with prominent darkening of palmar creases, a classic manifestation of primary adrenal insufficiency in autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome type 2. B: Clinical photograph of patient's lower legs and feet showing hyperpigmented, dry skin consistent with diffuse hyperpigmentation of primary adrenal insufficiency. C: Clinical photograph of patient's face showing facial hyperpigmentation, consistent with generalized hyperpigmentation of primary adrenal insufficiency.
panels.attribution_text: Pandya et al. Autoimmune Polyglandular Syndrome Type 2 With Hurthle Cell Adenoma: A Rare Association.. Cureus 2025. doi:10.7759/cureus.92931. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Patient profile on admission The patient had generalized hyperpigmentation, darkening of creases on the palms of the hand, and a cachectic look.
in_text_mentions: On admission, he had borderline low blood pressure with orthostatic hypotension and tachycardia, and he appeared dehydrated. On general examination, he had hyperpigmented, dry skin, a firm, mobile 2x1.5 cm nodule in the lower part of the right lobe of the thyroid gland with no lymphadenopathy (Figure 1). He had no signs suggestive of either hyper- or hypothyroidism. The rest of the systemic examination had been unremarkable.
